content: Silence is a lesson learned from the many sorrows of life.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Tranquillitate Animi (On Tranquility of Mind)
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Loneliness is the painful ache of feeling incomplete, while solitude is the rich discovery of your own inner presence. In a world full of constant stimulation and notifications, being alone with your thoughts can feel intimidating.

Seneca understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Yet silence is the only space where you can hear what your life is actually trying to say to you. When you make peace with quiet, you stop running to distractions to save you from yourself.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
